evidence.source: 金真姬, 常用漢字二百字探源
evidence.field: 手字形探源; 字義探源
evidence.text: The study states that 手 is not seen in oracle-bone inscriptions and that 金文編 records eleven forms. It describes the bronze graph as a hand, with finger branches above and an arm below; it identifies the basic meaning as human hand and treats Shuowen’s 拳 (“fist”) as an extended sense. The page’s form table includes 昌壺 under Western Zhou and later Zhou and manuscript forms.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.text: The page catalogs 手 forms from Western Zhou middle-period bronzes including 逆鐘 (集成63), 無㠱簋, and 曶壺蓋 (集成9728), then Western Zhou late-period bronzes, Warring States Chu and Qin forms, Qin slips, Han slips, and later clerical forms. These labels date the cited artifact traditions, but the page does not give semantic contexts for the cited bronze occurrences.
evidence.title: 手字形演變_手的甲骨文_手的金文_手的篆文_寫法_手字源圖片

evidence.source: 許慎, 說文解字 (quotation as reproduced by 書法圖集)
evidence.text: The page quotes 手，拳也。象形。凡手之屬皆从手。𠂿，古文手。 This is a historical lexicographic account; it does not independently establish the spoken-word history or a dated sequence of senses.
evidence.title: 手字形演變_手的甲骨文_手的金文_手的篆文_寫法_手字源圖片

It is therefore a derivative modern illustration rather than a directly attested 手 form; not selected as a historical glyph candidate.

search_audit.query: 手 字形演變 金文 西周 中期 手 甲骨文 absent pictograph; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File: 手-seal.svg; site:xiaoxuetang.ancientbooks.cn 手 字形演變 CC0
search_audit.outcome: Searched and opened a scholarly paleographic study, a character-specific form chart, exact Commons descriptions for seal, bronze and great-seal candidates, the Sinica and NTU records, and the official Unihan endpoint. The Unicode endpoint returned an internal error. Commons supplied actual direct SVG links; seal and bronze File pages establish identity and rights, while the direct bronze SVG fetch failed on unsupported image content type.

gaps: The inspected paleographic study reports no oracle-bone 手 graph and identifies bronze forms, including a Western Zhou form, but no directly dated earliest inscription with its semantic context was verified.

Graphic anatomy is an interpretation: the source describes five finger branches and an arm; an alternative cited dossier account mentions fingers, palm and arm. No photographed inscription was visually examined in this research stage.

The cited bronze examples establish forms and approximate artifact-period labels, not independently dated semantic uses. The early hand sense is supported by later lexicography and the study’s analysis, not by a located excavated text context.

Classical examples and later extensions in the dossier remain transmitted dictionary citations; this search did not independently establish dates or a chronological semantic pathway for skilled person, handwriting, or ‘hold’. Shuowen’s gloss 拳 is not a chronology.
No component or phonetic element is proposed for this pictographic graph. The deeper Sino-Tibetan, Burmese and 收 comparisons in the dossier were not independently verified in this search.

The exact Commons images are modern redrawings. The bronze direct SVG endpoint was verified as a link on the description page but could not be fetched by the web tool. No selected image is represented as an artifact photograph.

The official per-character Unihan record did not load. The local kMandarin reading row is available in the input but cannot be cited as externally inspected evidence; no phonological claim depends on it.

items.period: Western Zhou (style label on modern redraw; bronze forms are documented in the cited paleographic chart from Western Zhou middle period onward)
items.caption: A modern redraw labeled as a Western Zhou bronze-script form of 手. Bronze examples in paleographic catalogues show a recognizable hand graph; the file is not a photograph of an inscription.
items.alt: Modern vector redraw of 手 in a Western Zhou bronze inscription style.
items.selection_reason: Shows an early documented graphic form that the paleographic discussion interprets as a hand, while labeling the image honestly as a redraw.
items.rights: Commons description page states public-domain release for the modern drawing.

items.period: Qin/Han small-seal tradition as represented in the Shuowen seal-script style; the file is a modern redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of 手 in Shuowen seal-script style. Shuowen classifies it as pictographic; the image illustrates a later standardized representation, not an ancient artifact.
items.alt: Modern vector drawing of 手 in seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Pairs a later seal-script representation with the bronze-style redraw to explain continuity without claiming either image is an artifact photograph.
items.rights: Commons description page states public-domain release of the drawing and links the source form; source-page terms apply to that specific glyph image.

limitations.text: The bronze-style image’s direct SVG could not be fetched by the web tool, although its exact Commons description page establishes the direct original-file link, graph identity, period label and reuse statement. Visual review remains for the downstream image inspection step.
手-bigseal.svg is excluded because its own Commons page says 手 is not attested in great-seal script and the drawing is extracted from 看’s radical.
